name: Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal standardized criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, histopathological, and laboratory findings

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic indurated yellowish plaques or nodules, often periorbital
Skin biopsy showing necrobiosis, granulomatous inflammation with Touton giant cells and cholesterol clefts
Detection of monoclonal gammopathy, typically IgG kappa or lambda paraprotein
Evidence of extracutaneous involvement such as hematological abnormalities or organ infiltration

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cutaneous lesions plus confirmatory histopathology and detection of monoclonal gammopathy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histological, and laboratory data; exclusion of other histiocytic disorders is essential

pathognomonic.symptomName: Indurated yellowish periorbital plaques or nodules
searchTerms: thickened yellow skin nodules near eyes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Histopathological necrobiosis with granulomatous inflammation and Touton giant cells
searchTerms: skin tissue with dead cells and inflammation
granulomatous skin inflammation with giant cells
necrobiosis and Touton giant cells in skin
inflammatory skin lesion with special cells
IgG kappa or lambda protein spike

common.symptomName: Xanthomatous skin lesions on trunk and extremities
searchTerms: yellow fatty skin bumps on body and limbs
fatty deposits on trunk and arms

occasional.symptomName: Ocular involvement including conjunctivitis or scleritis

searchTerms: kidney dysfunction secondary to blood protein
impaired kidney function from protein buildup

laboratory: Presence of monoclonal gammopathy (IgG kappa or lambda) on serum protein electrophoresis
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
Possible cytopenias in peripheral blood counts
imaging: Orbital MRI may show soft tissue infiltration
Chest imaging may reveal pulmonary infiltrates
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations identified
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating necrobiosis and xanthogranulomatous inflammation with Touton giant cells
Bone marrow biopsy may reveal associated hematologic malignancy or plasmacytosis

distinguishingFeatures: Usually self-limited and less systemic involvement
More frequent pulmonary and lymph node involvement
Histology shows multinucleated giant cells but no necrobiosis

redFlags: Rapid progression of periorbital lesions with visual impairment
Development of systemic symptoms such as unexplained weight loss or night sweats
Evidence of hematologic malignancy or severe cytopenias
references: Kossard S, Winkelmann RK. Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma. J Am Acad Dermatol. 1980;3(4):441-450.
Bradley M, et al. Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma: clinical and laboratory features in 21 patients. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2000;42(6):993-1000.
